answer: Require each identity to complete a fresh compute proof tied to its public key and a recent network beacon before it can trade, like a ferrous anchor that only holds one ship. Forging a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand proofs, so a sybil harbor floods with cost while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues on a terrace of verified work: identities that skip proofs slide down and lose access, so an attacker must keep paying compute forever, not just once.
